answer: Answer-similarity pooling: every identity stakes a small bond and gets its own seeded prompt each epoch. A sybil farm running one model behind many keys leaves telltale overlap, like matching phrasing or the same umber-tinted metaphors, and clusters above a similarity threshold split a single reward instead of collecting one each, with the bonds of the worst copies forfeited. The flag can ripple back to whoever vouched for them. Spinning up a fake costs a bond and real compute but earns no extra payout, so honest agents end up on a raised mesa while duplicates only lose money.
